bearings.paper_claim: PoliPers defines 15 facets. Table 1 maps Assertiveness & Will to take control to AG: Assertiveness and Empathy & Compassion to COM: Warmth, and gives each facet a named opposite pole (Empathy's is Apathy & Indifference).
bearings.system_side: The persona codebook in agency_communion_llm.py uses the PoliPers names for its two cue classes and scores only the positive poles. The codebook names Birkenmaier & Lechner 2025 as its source. PoliPers does not cite that paper (it cites Repke, Birkenmaier & Lechner 2024, a survey-guide reference), so the link runs through shared authorship, not through PoliPers' citations.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The facet definitions transfer as construct definitions. The psychometric evidence does not: it comes from German survey ratings of traits, not from LLM coding of English congressional sentences.
bearings.verifier_note: Facet names, Agency/Communion mapping and opposite poles confirmed in Table 1 and pp.17-21. Corrected provenance: PoliPers does not cite Birkenmaier & Lechner 2025. Code line numbers in the original bearing were off; the codebook starts at line 31 and the positive-pole rule is at line 56.

bearings.paper_claim: The Assertiveness facet is not unidimensional. In ideal-politician ratings (Study 3, N=589) it gave two factors because the 'power-hungry, claims leadership' item loaded reversed, and its alpha was not computed (Table A4). In observer ratings of Trump and Merkel (pooled, Study 4, N=211) its alpha was .40 and omega .48 (Table A7). In ideal ratings Assertiveness was the only facet that differed by politician gender (d=.19, p=.025).
bearings.paper_location: pp.28-30; Table A4 p.70; Table A5 p.74; Table A7 p.79
bearings.system_side: The self-test treats 'I claim leadership and I am not afraid to use power to get results' as a gold agency unit. The sentence-level agency share pools all agency-labelled sentences, including power-claiming ones, into one score.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The split was measured in citizen ratings of traits, not in congressional sentences. Whether power-claiming and leadership-taking cues split in text is untested, so this is a plausibility warning, not a measured defect.
bearings.verifier_note: All numbers confirmed. Table A7 is captioned 'Study 3, real politicians' although it reports Study 4 observer data, and the paper's study labels are inconsistent throughout. The alpha .40 is pooled across the two targets, not a Trump-only or Merkel-only figure.

bearings.paper_claim: Observer correlations in Table 5 (Trump n=104, Merkel n=107, Study 4, Apr 2021): Empathy with likeability r=.70 (Trump) and .76 (Merkel); Integrity with ideological proximity r=.46 (Trump) and .36 (Merkel); Intellect with proximity r=.48 (Trump). All proximity correlations are positive as printed. PoliPers tests no link from any facet to behavior under pressure.
bearings.system_side: persona_susc_z = .60 z(communion) minus .40 z(agency), blended into susceptibility at PERSONA_W 0.30. The design presumes communal rhetoric marks susceptibility and assertive rhetoric marks resistance to pressure.
bearings.code_ref: fec/members/receptivity_layer.py:139-156 (persona channel and sign rationale), 186-191 (blend into susceptibility)
bearings.transfer_conditions: The correlations come from observers rating two foreign leaders on same-occasion ratings. They do not bear on how members of Congress respond to lobbying. Nothing here validates or refutes the persona signs, and the sign of the proximity association is unresolved (see verifier note).
bearings.verifier_note: Numbers confirmed against Table 5; the likeability column is the first Trump column and the first Merkel column in the extracted table. The proximity correlations are positive as printed, yet the paper's text says raters far from a politician rate the politician more negatively, which implies a negative sign. The paper does not reconcile this, so the bearing should report magnitudes and the printed sign only, and should not assert a bias direction. 'Partisan-tinged' is analyst wording; the paper speaks of ideological proximity.

bearings.paper_claim: Observer trait ratings track the rater's ideological proximity (r=.36-.48 on Integrity, Intellect and Creativity) and global evaluation (facet-likeability r up to .76). The authors read this as raters being less objective depending on where they stand politically, and separate positivity from descriptive normativity.
bearings.system_side: The LLM reader removes names, titles and party before scoring (deidentify), and the CT-CM model adds an LLM method factor to absorb judge halo.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper establishes the human-rater analogue only. That the same bias holds for an LLM's reputational priors is an inference. The CT-CM outcome is a separate matter and is not supported by this paper.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers and interpretation confirmed. The bearing's claim that CT-CM was a one-look MISS was not checked against any run output in this pass; the code docstring defines the bars but not the result, so that clause is removed from the transfer note. The proximity sign issue in the bearing above applies here too.

bearings.paper_claim: Observer trait ratings of politicians carry rater-ideology bias (proximity r up to .48). Several 4-item facets have low self-rating reliability (alpha .44-.52: Compromise .51, Humility .46, Loyalty .44, Creativity .45), which limits attainable convergent correlations.
bearings.system_side: Senate insider and academic expert panels are treated as independent gold criteria, and a halo PC1 bifactor removal (P2) was tested against the criteria.
bearings.code_ref: fec/members/build_big5_senate_gold.py:20,49 (insider and academic panel split), fec/members/big5_improvements_eval.py:186-187 (behavior panel and LEP criteria), 244-252 (P2 bars)
bearings.transfer_conditions: PoliPers raters were crowdworkers rating two prominent leaders, not experts rating senators, so the bias evidence is a reason to check panel ratings for partisanship, not proof that they are biased. The limit on convergent correlations is the analyst's inference from reliability.
bearings.verifier_note: The original code_ref is wrong. The Senate expert panel is built in build_big5_senate_gold.py (insiders n=129, academics n=125). The cited eval lines test against the behavior panel and LEP criteria, plus MTMM and known-groups bars, not against the expert panel. The bearing should say P2 was tested against the behavior and LEP criteria. Reliability figures confirmed in Table 2.

bearings.paper_claim: Global Big Five domains lack political specificity, and contextualized measures outperform non-contextualized ones. Facets diverge within a domain: Compromise with Agreeableness r=.33 versus Trust r=.50, and Intellect with Emotional Stability r=.41, which the authors call unexpected.
bearings.system_side: Five domain-level z scores are built from closed-vocabulary category rates with linear correlate weights, z-scored within the corpus.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The argument concerns survey item design, not text features. A facet-level text reader would need its own validation, and this paper does not change the domain-level validity record.
bearings.verifier_note: Table 3 values confirmed (Trust-A .50, Compromise-A .33, Empathy-A .48, Intellect-ES .41). The contextualization claim is in the introduction. The code side describes the domain weight table as written; the z-scoring step was not checked.

related.why: Shared authorship (Birkenmaier, Lechner). PoliPers does not cite this 2025 paper; it cites Repke, Birkenmaier & Lechner 2024. The paper title matches the agency and communion text-cue work the codebook ports, but its content was not re-read here.

PoliPers cites the main article (Rice, Remmel & Mondak 2020) for expert ratings of senators, not this appendix. This appendix is the source of the Senate insider and academic gold panel built in build_big5_senate_gold.py. The PoliPers proximity-bias finding concerns citizen raters, not experts.
PoliPers builds its facets hierarchically from the BFI-2 framework (Soto & John 2017) and validates them against the BFI-2-XS (Study 2, Table 3).

PoliPers cites Amsalem, Zoizner, Sheafer, Walgrave & Loewen (2020, Communication Research) for media visibility in its use-case discussion (around pp.37-38). The vault slug year is 2018 but the title matches. PoliPers does not state the direction of personality effects on visibility; the parenthetical in the original summary is not in PoliPers.

summary_issues: summary_md says the authors test the facets in four German samples, but Study 1 has no sample. Studies 2-4 give three samples: self-ratings N=404, ideal ratings N=589, observer ratings N=211.

summary_md says the paper supports de-identifying text before LLM rating and modeling halo as a method factor. PoliPers says nothing on either. It handles acquiescence by ipsatizing, and the halo method factor is the system's CT-CM design. Remove that sentence.
summary_md attributes a direction to Amsalem et al. (lower A, higher E/ES/O more covered). PoliPers cites Amsalem only for media visibility and does not state that direction. Drop the parenthetical.

Study labels in PoliPers are inconsistent. Tables 2 and 3 say Study 1 but report Study 2 self-ratings. Tables 4, 5 and A7 say Study 3 but report Study 4 observer ratings. Cite the text's numbering: Study 2 self, Study 3 ideal, Study 4 observer.

The rel's 'upstream source' of the facet labels is accurate, but the codebook's Birkenmaier & Lechner 2025 source is not cited in PoliPers. The provenance runs through shared authorship. State that in summary_md.
paul_entries is empty and no paul_markup was supplied, so paul_alignment cannot be checked against Paul's notes. Treat paul_alignment as unverified.

Dropped related links: ramey-2016-measuring-elite-personality (PoliPers does not cite it and cites Klingler, Hollibaugh & Ramey 2019 instead); rammstedt-2025-going-global-language (PoliPers cites the 2018 German BFI-2-XS validation, not this 2025 language-versions paper); byrne-2014-chokes-under-pressure (not cited by PoliPers; the link is system-side only).
Bearing 4 code_ref was wrong and is corrected above. The P2 halo test was run against behavior and LEP criteria, not the Senate expert panel.

All Table 5 proximity correlations are positive as printed, while the paper's text implies raters far from a politician rate it lower. This is unreconciled in the paper. Report the printed sign only and do not assert a bias direction in summary_md or the bearings.

Denominators are missing in summary_md. Add Study 2 N=404 (fieldwork Oct 2020, self-ratings, alpha .44-.87 across 15 facets), Study 3 N=589 (May 2020), and Study 4 N=211 pooled (Apr 2021; Trump n=104, Merkel n=107).
The CT-CM one-look MISS claim in the Study 3 bearing was not checked against any run output and is removed from the transfer note.

gaps_exposed and flags make system claims (for example Compromise approximated only by cooperation_v2; the no-validation statement for persona signs) that were not verified in this pass. The paper-side claim that no facet is linked to pressure response is confirmed.
